process.title: What happens when you ask
process.intro: You can ask for yourself, for your child, or for someone you care about. Here is what happens after you reach out.

steps.name: Submit a request
steps.text: Tell us a little about you and what you are living with. If we move forward, we will ask for photos and records later, through a secure system.

steps.name: Initial review
steps.text: Our team reads every request and considers whether surgery could help and whether it fits what our ministry can do.

steps.name: Conversation
steps.text: If we may be able to help, we will contact you to learn more and answer your questions.

steps.name: Decision
steps.text: We consider each request prayerfully, weighing medical need against the resources we have.

steps.name: Care and support
steps.text: If we move forward together, we stay with you through surgery and recovery, and long after it ends.

process.assurance: You will never be pressured, and what you share stays confidential. You can ask us questions at any point.
process.draftNote: These steps are a draft from the ministry's founding notes and will be confirmed before launch.

conditions.title: Who we help
conditions.intro: Children and adults in the Charlotte and Fort Mill area who need reconstructive plastic surgery they cannot afford. Care is free or offered at reduced cost.
conditions.faith: You do not need to share our faith to receive care. The ministry is open to everyone.

items.name: Scar repair and scar revision
items.text: Scars from injury, surgery or burns that limit movement or change how you look.

items.name: Facial differences and reconstruction
items.text: Facial deformity from injury, illness or birth, and surgery to restore form and function.

items.name: Birth defects and congenital differences
items.text: Conditions a person was born with, which doctors call congenital. Surgery can improve function and quality of life.

items.name: Cleft lip and cleft-related surgery
items.text: Care for cleft lip and the needs that come with it, including a revision as a child grows.

items.name: Injury and trauma reconstruction
items.text: Reconstruction after an accident or injury, to restore function and appearance.

items.name: Burn scars
items.text: Treatment for scarring or burn injuries that limit movement or change how you look.

items.name: Skin lesions or growths that affect appearance or function
items.text: Lesions or growths on the skin that change how you look or limit how part of your body works.

items.name: Breast reconstruction or deformity
items.text: Restoring form after cancer surgery or related treatment, and care for breast differences from birth or injury.

items.name: Abdominal wall and body changes
items.text: Changes to the abdominal wall and body after major weight loss, trauma or surgery.

items.name: Revision after previous surgery
items.text: Another operation to improve the result of an earlier one that still limits you.

items.name: Children with congenital or acquired differences
items.text: Children born with a difference, or who have one from injury or illness. A parent or guardian asks on their behalf.

items.name: Something else
items.text: If your need is not listed here, ask anyway. We consider each request on its own.

conditions.title: Conditions we help with
conditions.intro: We look at each need on its own. Here are the conditions people ask about, in everyday words and in the terms doctors use. If yours is not here, ask anyway.
conditions.footnote: Our care is reconstructive and restorative, aimed at function, form and healing. We do not offer cosmetic procedures.

paragraphs.text: Care is free or offered at a reduced cost you can manage. We talk through any cost with you before anything is decided.

items.text: A few words about what you are living with
A safe way to reach you

That is all for now. You do not need to send photos or records yet. If we move forward, we will ask for them later, through a secure system. Records help if you have them, but you do not need any to ask.

paragraphs.text: What you send us is health information, and we protect it that way. Only the ministry’s care team reads requests. We never sell your information. If we move forward, we ask for photos and records through a secure system, and we use them only to review your care.
There are no advertising or tracking tools on the pages where you ask for help.

items.a: Scars and burn scars, facial differences, birth defects and other congenital differences, cleft lip, injuries, skin lesions or growths that affect appearance or function, breast reconstruction, changes after major weight loss, and revision after previous surgery. Children are included. The ministry’s care is reconstructive and restorative, so we don’t offer cosmetic procedures. If you aren’t sure your need fits, ask anyway.

items.q: Do you offer charitable plastic surgery or pro bono reconstructive surgery?
items.a: The ministry provides reconstructive plastic surgery free or at reduced cost for people whose need exceeds their means. We talk through any cost with you before anything is decided.

items.q: Is there a reconstructive plastic surgeon in Fort Mill or Charlotte who can help?
items.a: The ministry serves people in the Fort Mill, SC and Charlotte, NC area. Ask for help and we will talk with you about whether we are the right fit.

items.q: Do I need insurance, a referral or medical records?
items.a: No. Your insurance may be considered, so tell us if you have any. Each person is evaluated individually, based on medical need, financial circumstances, available resources, and our ability to safely provide care. Records are optional. If you have them, we will ask for them later, through a secure system, because they help us. You never need them to ask, and the names of doctors you’ve seen help too.
Only if you’d like. We offer prayer to every patient, and saying no never affects your care.

items.q: Who decides whether I can receive care?
items.a: Our team considers each request prayerfully, weighing medical need, the resources we have, and what our volunteer surgeons are able to do. If you live outside the Charlotte and Fort Mill area, ask anyway.

items.q: How long until I hear back?
items.a: We let you know we’ve received your request. We generally respond to initial requests within 5–7 business days.
We’ll tell you plainly, and where we can, we’ll point you toward other care.

items.q: Can I ask by phone, or in Spanish?
items.a: Yes to both. Call us and we’ll go through the request with you, in English or Spanish. A Spanish version of this site is on the way.

items.text: An active, unrestricted license to practice in North Carolina or South Carolina.
Board certification or eligibility for surgeons and anesthesiologists.
Proof of malpractice coverage, or coverage arranged through the ministry.
A background check and HIPAA training before your first surgery day.

paragraphs.title: Time
paragraphs.text: Serve when you can: a single surgery day, a few days a year, or on a regular schedule.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.lede: How Beauty From Ashes Surgical Ministry collects, uses and protects the information you share through this website.
privacy.draft: This notice is a draft. The ministry will publish its final privacy notice, including a HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices, after legal review.

paragraphs.text: We collect what you choose to send through the forms on this site: requests for care, referrals, volunteer and partner forms, and messages. Requests and referrals can include health information. If we move forward, we ask for photos and records separately, through a secure system.
Like most websites, our host keeps basic server records, such as the date of a visit and the type of browser used.
We use your information to review requests for care, to contact you, and to coordinate volunteers and partners. We never sell your information, and we never use it for advertising.

Requests for care and referrals are protected health information under HIPAA. They are sent through a HIPAA-compliant service that has signed a Business Associate Agreement with the ministry, and only the ministry’s care team can see them.
This site uses no advertising or tracking cookies. Its fonts load from this site, so visiting does not report you to a font service.
If the ministry adds visitor statistics in the future, they will never run on the pages where you ask for help or refer someone.
You can ask to see, correct or delete the information you’ve sent us. Contact us by phone or email and we’ll respond within 30 days.
A parent or legal guardian sends requests for care for anyone under 18.
Questions about this notice? Contact the ministry by phone or email.

privacy.updated: Last updated: draft, not yet in effect.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.lede: Everyone should be able to learn about the ministry and ask for help, including people who use screen readers, keyboards, magnification or voice control.

paragraphs.text: We build and test this site against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA. Accessibility is built into the site itself. We don’t use overlay widgets.

items.text: Every page works with a keyboard alone, with visible focus.
Form fields have labels, and errors say what to fix.
Forms have no time limits.
Text can be enlarged to 200%, and pages reflow at 400% zoom.
Animation stops when your device asks for reduced motion.
Pages work in high-contrast modes.

paragraphs.text: The Spanish translation is in progress, so some pages show English until it’s complete.
Call or email us and we’ll help you another way, including taking a request for care over the phone. Please tell us what got in your way so we can fix it.
